model_reported.name: conduire-experience-optimisation
model_reported.summary: Proposed a single four-lane scalar-interleaving experiment with independent per-pixel state and a scalar remainder.

model_reported.name: inspecter-environnement
model_reported.summary: Used the supplied target/compiler context and avoided ISA-specific assumptions; no extra environment inspection was performed.

model_reported.name: consulter-documentation-technique
model_reported.summary: The experiment uses ordinary scalar C++ arithmetic and introduces no uncertain API, instruction, or library behavior.

model_reported.name: evaluer-performances
model_reported.summary: Reported the available baseline measurement and correctness record without claiming an unmeasured speedup; one-thread and four-core-budget results remain to be measured.

memory_lessons.applicability: The only available measurement is a correct sequential baseline; it does not provide separate one-thread and four-core-budget timings, so comparisons should report matched-budget measurements explicitly.
memory_lessons.claim: The baseline passed 8 correctness cases and had a measured mean of 0.563421510301172 seconds; no interleaved variants are yet present in the catalog.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure this four-lane candidate against the baseline at one thread and report the four-core-budget result separately.

proposal.hypothesis: Interleaving four independent scalar pixel states may expose instruction-level parallelism and reduce recurrence dependency stalls. The per-lane escape checks and recurrence order remain unchanged; lanes with different escape lengths and the scalar tail may reduce or eliminate any benefit.

retained: Process complete groups of four adjacent pixels with named scalar state variables interleaved across iterations.
Track each lane's active state independently so each pixel retains its own escape count despite differing escape lengths.
Use the original scalar Mandelbrot routine for the non-divisible row tail and retain complete output overwrite behavior.
